package_info.package_manager: bundled with freeware (not a traditional package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Fireball is considered malicious because it hijacks web browsers to manipulate browser settings, change DNS, and can execute arbitrary code or download additional malware, enabling both monetization and further compromise of infected systems.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon browser launch or system startup)
execution_context.file_location: browser configuration files / registry entries / browser extensions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Modifies browser default homepage and search engine settings to attacker-controlled values.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (could be JavaScript, registry scripts, or binary code depending on infection vector)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code alters browser configuration files or registry entries to set the homepage and search engine to attacker-controlled URLs, redirecting user traffic and search queries for monetization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing browser settings without user consent is a hallmark of browser hijackers and adware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not alter browser settings without explicit user permission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may set browser defaults for policy compliance, but with user or admin awareness.
key_indicators: Redirection to non-standard search engines or homepages

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial infection or on browser events)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Executes arbitrary code or downloads and runs additional malware payloads from remote servers.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (could be shellcode, JavaScript, or binary payloads)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware executes arbitrary code or downloads additional malware from attacker-controlled servers, enabling further compromise or monetization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to execute arbitrary code or download further malware is a critical security risk and a common trait of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal browser extensions or software should not have the capability to execute arbitrary code or download and run untrusted binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download updates, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.
key_indicators: Download and execution of unsigned binaries

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Manipulates browser content and DNS settings to redirect traffic or inject advertisements.
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (JavaScript, system scripts, or binary code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies browser content and DNS settings to redirect user traffic or inject advertisements, monetizing user activity and potentially exposing users to further threats.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DNS and content manipulation for ad injection or redirection is a classic sign of adware and browser hijackers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not alter DNS settings or inject ads into browser sessions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parental control or security software may filter DNS, but with user awareness and consent.

attack_chain.action: Malware is installed on the victim's machine via bundling with freeware.
On execution, the malware modifies browser settings to hijack homepage and search engine.
attack_chain.leads_to: User traffic and search queries are redirected for monetization

attack_chain.action: Malware manipulates browser content and DNS settings to inject ads or redirect traffic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased ad revenue and potential exposure to further threats

attack_chain.action: Malware executes arbitrary code or downloads additional payloads from remote servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further compromise of the system or installation of more malware

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage or search engine settings
Injection of advertisements into web pages
Execution of code or download of binaries from untrusted remote servers
file_indicators: Altered browser configuration files (e.g., prefs.js for Firefox, registry keys for Chrome/IE)
Presence of unknown browser extensions or plugins
Unexpected scripts or binaries in browser or system directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known adware or malware command-and-control domains
Unusual DNS queries or changes to DNS server settings
HTTP/HTTPS requests to download additional payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to browser settings, unexpected browser extensions, and modifications to DNS configurations. Analyze network traffic for connections to known malicious domains and for downloads of executable files from untrusted sources. Use endpoint protection to detect unauthorized code execution and browser hijacking behaviors.
